clue.text: Supporters having no right to become such addicts

indicators.note: the supporters lack something, so a letter is taken away from their word

parts.note: friends are people who back you up

explanation.surface: Fans who have lost their moral compass turn into fanatics.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend can be an addict or devotee, as in a dope fiend or a fresh-air fiend.

clue.text: Informative response not going beyond characters in first eleven

parts.words: not going beyond characters in first eleven
parts.note: every letter of the answer comes from the first eleven letters of the alphabet, A to K

explanation.surface: A coach's useful comments on players who never get past the first team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First eleven' suggests a cricket or football team, but it means the alphabet's first eleven letters, A to K; FEEDBACK uses only those.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is comment given in reply to someone's work or performance, telling them how it went.

clue.text: I led a riot badly, as leader

indicators.note: the words are put together poorly, so their letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A confession from someone who led a riot poorly while in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like it describes a person in charge of the riot, but it is a newspaper's leading article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the main opinion column, the paper's editorial.

clue.text: Tracks guided traveller in frozen North

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or track them
led means guided

explanation.surface: Someone was guided along a trail through the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-drawn sled is how people have long travelled across Arctic snow and ice.

clue.text: Got to the bottom of what's feminine in diamonds

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for feminine
being in means being at home
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone discovered what womanliness has to do with diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in diamonds' looks like an insertion, but 'in' stands for AT HOME and simply follows F.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to understand it fully, measuring its depth like a sounding line.

clue.text: What can be included repeatedly at OU?

definitions.text: What can be included repeatedly at OU?

indicators.note: says the letters are capable of being turned into something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
repeatedly says the word at is used twice, followed by OU as written

explanation.surface: A question about what the Open University takes in over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles AT, and the letters of INCLUDED, AT, AT and OU are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer. The OU is Britain's Open University, a distance-learning institution for mature students.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses for grown-ups returning to study are exactly the business of the Open University.

clue.text: Old in hospital taking advantage of accommodation

indicators.note: the old letter is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
using someone is taking advantage of them

explanation.surface: An elderly patient exploits the hospital as a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing is the general term for dwellings and places where people are lodged.

clue.text: The writer, a kung fu expert, got in scrappy fight

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
Bruce Lee was the famous martial-arts film star

explanation.surface: The author and a martial artist ended up in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused hand-to-hand scuffle involving many people.

clue.text: Remove damp from study for old poet

parts.note: to dry something is to take the moisture out of it
a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: Clearing mildew from a room once used by a bygone poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the seventeenth-century English Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Tasteless dissension around king in some quarters, perhaps

parts.note: vulgar means lacking taste

indicators.note: the dissension word goes around the king's letter

parts.note: faction can mean internal strife or discord within a group
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Crude infighting surrounds the monarch in certain parts of the realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' suggests districts, but here it means fractions such as three quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgar fraction is one written as numerator over denominator, like three quarters.

clue.text: Having a view, for example, about female principle

indicators.note: the example letters go about, around, the principle

parts.note: yin is the female principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Holding an opinion on the feminine principle, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something is looking at it, having it in sight.

clue.text: Students collectively, in universities, join together on rare occasions

indicators.note: the students' letters sit inside the universities' letters

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, doubled for the plural
NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' body
to ally is to unite

explanation.surface: The student union joins forces with universities only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done unusually happens seldom, out of the ordinary run of things.

clue.text: Illegally distributed to give profit to member

parts.note: boot is an archaic verb meaning to profit or avail, as in 'what boots it?'
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Pirated goods sold to give someone a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg goods, such as liquor or recordings, are made and sold unlawfully.

clue.text: Expend my energy, crossing river in old boat

indicators.note: the river letter cuts across the phrase, sitting within it

parts.note: tire me means wear me out
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Rowing across a river in an ancient vessel wears me out.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient Greek or Roman warship with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Digs choir I led, arranged around piano — people like a little Mozart

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters go around the piano's letter
the words are set out in a new order, so their letters are reshuffled

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A choirmaster's lodgings, songs arranged round a piano, and a young Mozart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' sounds musical, fitting the choir and piano, but it is the signal to reshuffle DIGS CHOIR I LED.
explanation.definitionFit: The young Mozart, performing at five, is the classic example of a gifted child genius.

clue.text: Support, putting in time for Conservative followers

indicators.note: one letter is put into the word in place of another
the time letter stands for, replaces, the Conservative letter

parts.note: to encourage is to support

explanation.surface: Backing a party by swapping Tories for a fresh term, with supporters in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants who follow an important person around.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement embraced by foremost English novelist

indicators.note: the movement word is held within the other pieces

parts.note: top means foremost
a roll is a turning-over movement

explanation.surface: A leading English writer caught up in a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics, but it describes a rolling movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was the Victorian author of the Barsetshire novels.

clue.text: One depends on current supply as source of rock

definitions.text: One depends on current supply as source of rock

parts.words: One depends on current supply as source of rock
parts.note: an amplified instrument needs electricity to play, and it drives rock music

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' and 'rock' suggest a stream and geology; they mean electric current and rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument relies on mains power through an amplifier and is the backbone of rock bands.

clue.text: Group of Roman soldiers almost capturing a horseman, so to speak?

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the letter inside it
the word stops short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a century was a Roman army unit of about a hundred men

explanation.surface: Roman troops nearly seized a cavalryman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a centaur is less a rider than half-man, half-horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur in Greek myth has a man's torso on a horse's body, literally a horse-man.

clue.text: Do without top ointment

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a do is a party or function

explanation.surface: Managing without the best skin cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is anointing with oil, and by extension the oil or salve used.

clue.text: It can be got from tree, primarily medicinal

definitions.text: It can be got from tree, primarily medicinal

parts.note: balsa is a tropical American tree with very light wood

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A remedy that comes from a tree and is mainly used to heal.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is an aromatic resin obtained from certain trees and used in soothing remedies.

clue.text: Annual publication from local man, a calendar

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A yearly book produced by a man from the area, a datebook.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a book issued every year with calendars, dates and statistics.

clue.text: Missing British spy chief at Pentagon, say

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
at and in both indicate location
the Pentagon is the US defence headquarters, standing for the US

explanation.surface: An MI6 boss has gone missing while visiting the American defence headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus as an adjective or preposition means lacking or without.

clue.text: With start of therapy, getting real about feelings

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: actual means real

explanation.surface: Starting therapy and getting honest about one's emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feelings' suggests emotions, but it means the sense of touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactual means relating to touch, the sense by which things are felt.

clue.text: Resort for Romanians in enclave inside Italy

indicators.note: the letters are sorted again, re-sorted, into a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday destination for Romanians in a pocket of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a holiday spot but means re-sort, the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic completely surrounded by Italian territory.

clue.text: Final stage appearance as Shakespearean villain grabbing maiden

indicators.note: the villain takes hold of the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Iago is the schemer in Othello
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An actor's last scene as Iago, seizing a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage appearance' suggests theatre, but the definition is an insect's last stage of development.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the fully developed adult form of an insect, after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Character fault one's shown in mile race

indicators.note: these letters appear within the other pieces

parts.note: a sprint is a short fast race
one gives the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for 'is', joining it to the rest

explanation.surface: A runner's personality flaw is revealed in a mile race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests personality, but it means a printed letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is an error in a printed character, a typographical slip.

clue.text: Queen accepting European vote as constructive addition

indicators.note: the queen takes on the following letters after her name

parts.note: Queen Anne, the last Stuart monarch
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: The Queen takes a European vote as a helpful extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructive' sounds like helpful, but it points to building: an annexe is a built extension.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension or extra building attached to a main one.
